rows.verbatim:
B. Limits on Use of Site: Limit use of Project site to areas within the Contract limits indicated. Do
not disturb portions of the Project site beyond areas in which Work is indicated.
1. The Contractor is responsible for the security of the Contractor’s equipment and materials.
2. Schedule deliveries to minimize on-site storage of materials and equipment.
3. Existing materials and equipment that are removed as part of the construction operations,
and that are not reused or salvaged as Government property, shall become the property of
the Contractor and shall be promptly removed from the site.
4. Utilities are available near the site for construction purposes. The Chapel Hill Beach area
has electric, water, and sewer utilities. This is located approximately 3 miles from the Wild
Boar Ridge Campground. The water service at Chapel Hill Beach is closed in September
and reopened in April.
5. The site will be open to the public for use during construction. Care will be exercised to
adhere to the schedule and to secure the Government facility after hours. The Contractor
will be responsible for signing, limiting access, and safety of public and/or government
employees in the area.
6. Keep driveways, loading areas, and entrances serving premises clear and available to
Owner, Owner’s employees, and emergency vehicles at all times. Do not use these areas
for parking or storage of materials.

the absorption current to attain reasonable stabilization (one minute minimum).
rows.normalized: If testing is applied in steps, contractor must increase uniformly with each step long enough for stabilization (one minute minimum).

rows.verbatim: Take current and voltage readings at the end of each step duration.
rows.normalized: Contractor must take current and voltage readings at the end of each step duration.

rows.verbatim: Plot leakage current in microamps DC vs. test voltage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must plot leakage current in microamps DC vs. test voltage.

rows.verbatim: Continue plot for five minutes.
rows.normalized: Contractor must continue the plot for five minutes.

rows.verbatim:
Correct point faults by enclosing fault area in cast in-line splice enclosure, WITHOUT
SPLICING.
rows.normalized: Contractor must correct point faults by enclosing fault area in a cast in-line splice enclosure without splicing.

rows.verbatim:
If wire is damaged remove and replace failed conductor with in-line compression
splice lugs and poured urethane splice as above.
rows.normalized: If wire is damaged, contractor must remove and replace the failed conductor with in-line compression splice lugs and poured urethane splice.

rows.verbatim: Install any splice or fault area described above in a splice vault or pedestal.
rows.normalized: Contractor must install any splice or fault area in a splice vault or pedestal.

rows.verbatim: Submit all test results in hard copy and PDF.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit all test results in hard copy and PDF.

rows.verbatim: Materials must be kept dry until ready to use.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep seed materials dry until ready to use.

rows.verbatim:
Seeds shall be from Missouri eco-types or, if unavailable, from adjacent states. Seeding
shall be at a rate recommended by the vendor.
rows.normalized: Seeds shall be from Missouri eco-types (or adjacent states if unavailable) and seeding shall be at the vendor-recommended rate.

rows.verbatim: Seeding shall be at a rate recommended by the vendor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall seed at the rate recommended by the vendor.

rows.verbatim: In areas where slope is greater than 35%, then an annual rye and/or winter wheat and weed free straw shall be applied at 50 pounds per acre.
rows.normalized: If slope is greater than 35%, contractor shall apply annual rye and/or winter wheat and weed-free straw at 50 pounds per acre.

rows.verbatim:
A. Product Data: For each type of product indicated
B. Product certificates.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit product data for each product type and product certificates.

rows.verbatim: Deliver, store and handle materials according to manufacturer’s recommendations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must deliver, store, and handle seed materials according to manufacturer's recommendations.

rows.verbatim:
A. Grass Seed: Fresh, clean, dry, new-crop seed complying with ASOA’s “Journal of Seed
Technology; Rules for Testing Seeds” for purity and germination tolerances.
rows.normalized: Grass seed must be fresh, clean, dry, new-crop seed complying with ASOA's Journal of Seed Technology rules for purity and germination tolerances.

rows.verbatim:
B. Grass Seed Mix – the following seed mixes will be used to stabilize the soil and revegetate the
site:
1. If applied during November through March:
Sites will be revegetated using a seed mix containing River Oats (Chasmanthium
latifolium), Little Bluestem (Schizachyrium scoparium), Showy Tickseed (Bidens
aristosa), Partridge Pea (Chamaecrista fasciculata), Lance-Leafed Coreopsis (Coreopsis
lanceolata), Wild Bergamot (Monarda fistulosa), Slender Mountain Mint (Pycnanthemum
tenuifolium), and Black-Eyed Susan (Rudbeckia hirta).
rows.normalized: If seeding is applied November through March, contractor must use a seed mix containing the specified eight native species.

rows.verbatim:
2. If applied during April through October:
Sites will be revegetated using an annual rye and/or winter wheat mixed with Little
Bluestem (Schizachyrium scoparium) applied at 50 pounds per acre.
rows.normalized: If seeding is applied April through October, contractor must use annual rye/winter wheat mixed with Little Bluestem applied at 50 pounds per acre.

rows.verbatim: Topsoil shall have a pH range of 5.5 to 7.4.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide topsoil with a pH range of 5.5 to 7.4

rows.verbatim:
Spread organic topsoil at a minimum depth of 4 inches over area to be planted and integrate with
the top layer of subsoil to prevent hardpan separation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must spread organic topsoil at a minimum depth of 4 inches and integrate with subsoil

rows.verbatim: Reuse surface soil on-site and amended topsoil from commercial sources.
rows.normalized: Contractor must reuse on-site surface soil and amended topsoil from commercial sources.

rows.verbatim:
Provide topsoil which is fertile, friable, natural loam, surface soil which is reasonably free of
subsoil, high clay content, brush, weeds, litter, stumps, rocks and any other material which may
be harmful to plant growth.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide topsoil that is fertile, friable, natural loam, free of harmful materials.

rows.verbatim:
NOTE: The C.O.R. shall approve the Contractor’s provided soil sample prior to installation and
planting
rows.normalized: Contractor's soil sample must be approved by the C.O.R. prior to installation and planting (contractor dependency).

rows.verbatim:
B. Mulches:
1. Straw Mulch: Provide air dry, clean, mildew- and seed-free, and certified weed-free
threshed straw of wheat, rye, oats, or barley.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide air-dry, clean, mildew- and seed-free, certified weed-free straw mulch of wheat, rye, oats, or barley.

rows.verbatim:
Grade planting areas to a smooth, uniform surface plane with loose, uniformly
fine texture.
rows.normalized: Contractor must grade planting areas to a smooth, uniform surface plane with loose, fine texture.

rows.verbatim: Grade to within plus or minus ½ inch of finish elevation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must grade to within plus or minus ½ inch of finish elevation.

rows.verbatim: Roll and rake, remove ridges, and fill depressions to meet finish grades.
rows.normalized: Contractor must roll and rake, remove ridges, and fill depressions to meet finish grades.

rows.verbatim: Limit fine grading to areas that can be planted in the immediate future.
rows.normalized: Contractor must limit fine grading to areas that can be planted in the immediate future.

rows.verbatim: Restore areas if eroded or otherwise disturbed after finish grading and before planting.
rows.normalized: If areas are eroded or disturbed after finish grading and before planting, contractor must restore them.

rows.verbatim: Scarify existing subsoil and compacted areas prior to spreading topsoil.
rows.normalized: Contractor must scarify existing subsoil and compacted areas prior to spreading topsoil.

rows.verbatim: Prepare subsoil to eliminate uneven areas.
rows.normalized: Contractor must prepare subsoil to eliminate uneven areas.

rows.verbatim: Maintain profiles and contours.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain profiles and contours.

rows.verbatim: Make changes in grade gradual.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make changes in grade gradual.

rows.verbatim: Blend slopes into level areas.
rows.normalized: Contractor must blend slopes into level areas.

rows.verbatim: Rake the surface smooth.
rows.normalized: Contractor must rake the surface smooth.

rows.verbatim: Place topsoil during dry weather and on dry, unfrozen subgrade.
rows.normalized: Contractor must place topsoil during dry weather and on dry, unfrozen subgrade.

rows.verbatim: Remove foreign, non-organic material from topsoil while spreading.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove foreign, non-organic material from topsoil while spreading.

rows.verbatim: Grade topsoil to eliminate rough, low or soft areas and to ensure positive drainage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must grade topsoil to eliminate rough, low, or soft areas and ensure positive drainage.

rows.verbatim: All seeded areas to receive a settled minimum depth of 4” of topsoil.
rows.normalized: All seeded areas shall receive a settled minimum depth of 4 inches of topsoil.

rows.verbatim: Remove foreign materials, weeds and undesirable pants and their roots.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove foreign materials, weeds, and undesirable plants and their roots.

rows.verbatim: Remove any contaminated subsoil if present.
rows.normalized: If contaminated subsoil is present, contractor must remove it.

rows.verbatim:
Prepare seeding areas by removing and/or killing off any unwanted existing vegetation with a
glyphosate herbicide, applied only by a state certified applicator no sooner than 2 weeks prior to
seed installation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must prepare seeding areas by removing/killing unwanted vegetation with glyphosate herbicide applied only by a state-certified applicator no sooner than 2 weeks prior to seed installation.

rows.verbatim: Soils surface should be loose and free of any soil clumps exceeding 1 inch in diameter.
rows.normalized: Soil surface should be loose and free of soil clumps exceeding 1 inch in diameter.

rows.verbatim:
Seed shall be installed by means of mechanical and/or hand broadcast methods to ensure even
distribution of seeds throughout all designated seeded areas.
rows.normalized: Seed shall be installed via mechanical and/or hand broadcast methods to ensure even distribution throughout designated seeded areas.

rows.verbatim: Native seed mix shall be mixed thoroughly by vendor/supplier at their recommended ratios.
rows.normalized: The vendor/supplier shall mix the native seed mix thoroughly at their recommended ratios.

rows.verbatim: Apply seed evenly in two intersecting directions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must apply seed evenly in two intersecting directions.

rows.verbatim: Rake in lightly, then lightly mulch with clean, weed free straw.
rows.normalized: Contractor must rake in lightly, then lightly mulch with clean, weed-free straw.

rows.verbatim:
Seeded areas shall be watered immediately following installation to accelerate cover crop
germination.
rows.normalized: Seeded areas shall be watered immediately following installation to accelerate germination.

rows.verbatim:
K. An acceptable quality seed installation is defined as having:
1. No bare spots larger than 1 square foot after substantial germination.
2. No more than 10% of the total area with bare spots larger than 1 square foot.
3. A uniform coverage throughout all seeded areas.
rows.normalized: An acceptable quality seed installation requires: no bare spots larger than 1 sq ft after substantial germination, no more than 10% of total area with bare spots larger than 1 sq ft, and uniform coverage.

rows.verbatim: Do not perform seeding in windy conditions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not perform seeding in windy conditions.

rows.verbatim: Surface layer of soil for seeded areas shall be kept moist throughout gemination period.
rows.normalized: The surface layer of soil for seeded areas shall be kept moist throughout the germination period.

rows.verbatim:
Mulch the areas with a light covering of clean, chopped straw to retain moisture and use a tackifier
to prevent wind damage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must mulch the areas with a light covering of clean, chopped straw and use a tackifier to prevent wind damage.

rows.verbatim:
If installed in spring, lightly water 4-6 weeks after germination at regular intervals (depending on
rainfall), or if an extended drought occurs throughout the summer months.
rows.normalized: If installed in spring, contractor must lightly water 4-6 weeks after germination at regular intervals, or if extended drought occurs during summer.

rows.verbatim:
Protect seeded areas from pedestrian traffic or vehicular trespassing with temporary fences, signs,
barriers, etc. while seed is germinating.
rows.normalized: Contractor must protect seeded areas from pedestrian/vehicular trespassing with temporary fences, signs, barriers while seed germinates.

rows.verbatim: Repair damage resulting from trespass, erosion, settlement, etc.
rows.normalized: Contractor must repair damage resulting from trespass, erosion, settlement, etc.

rows.verbatim: Remove temporary protective devices after final acceptance.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove temporary protective devices after final acceptance.

rows.verbatim:
Maintain seeded areas immediately after placement until vegetation is well established and
exhibits a vigorous growing condition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain seeded areas immediately after placement until vegetation is well established and vigorous.

rows.verbatim:
Control the growth of weeds to the extent possible by using various methods such as line
trimming, mowing and selective herbicide use.
rows.normalized: Contractor must control weed growth to the extent possible using line trimming, mowing, and selective herbicide use.

rows.verbatim: Apply herbicide in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must apply herbicide in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.

rows.verbatim: Contractor will be responsible for any damage resulting from improper use of herbicides.
rows.normalized: Contractor will be responsible for any damage resulting from improper use of herbicides.

rows.verbatim: Immediately reseed areas that show bare spots.
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately reseed areas that show bare spots.

rows.verbatim:
Well shall be pump tested to determine its maximum pumping rate at a stabilized drawdown which does not
exceed 1.5 times the design pumping rate (15 gpm) or the maximum amount the screen (if present) can
safely pass.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall pump test the well to determine maximum pumping rate at a stabilized drawdown not exceeding 1.5 times the design rate (15 gpm) or the safe screen capacity.

rows.verbatim:
This reading should be the same as the original static
water level. If not, continue time and recordings until the static water level has stabilized.
rows.normalized: If the 30-minute recovery reading is not the same as the original static water level, contractor must continue timing/recording until the water level stabilizes.

rows.verbatim: No longer working, leave in place.
rows.normalized: Contractor must leave the existing (non-working) generator in place.

rows.verbatim:
Contractor to connect new electric to existing electric control
panel to power new well pump.
rows.normalized: Contractor is required to connect new electric service to the existing electric control panel to power the new well pump.
